# Architecture

ULPF has a **data plane** (one Vector 0.58 process; generated configuration)
and a **control plane** (the `ulpf` Python CLI and the Streamlit UI). The
control plane never sits in the event path; it compiles, verifies, replays and
reports. OpenSearch 3.8 stores the searchable copy. Everything runs as the
invoking non-root user, bound to 127.0.0.1 by default (ADR-002).

## Data plane (generated by `ulpf spec compile` → `pipeline/vector/generated/vector-live.yaml`)

```
SOURCES (bytes codec — no decoding, no syslog parsing at intake)
  in_syslog_udp   socket udp   127.0.0.1:5514
  in_syslog_tcp   socket tcp   127.0.0.1:5514   newline frames, max 1 MiB
  in_syslog_tls   socket tcp   127.0.0.1:6514   TLS (deployment CA) — when deploy/certs exists
  in_syslog_tcp_octet          RFC 6587 octet counting — OFF by default (finding V20)
  in_http         http_server  127.0.0.1:8088   NDJSON lines
  in_inbox        file         runtime/data/inbox/*.log
        │ tag_* (transport, peer)
        ▼
  ulpf_envelope        event_uid = UUIDv7(receipt time), ingest {time ns, collector, transport, peer},
                       raw {sha256, len, utf8}; raw bytes travel in ._raw
        ├──► ulpf_archive_record ─► ulpf_archive_batch (reduce ≤1000/≤0.5 s) ─► out_archive  (file)
        ▼
  ulpf_preparse        layers: PRI, syslog (RFC 3164/5424, header ts as written), CEF, LEEF 1/2,
                       JSON, KV, CSV, text; .ulpf.format, .ulpf.fingerprint; oversize guard
  ulpf_match           generated: first matching approved spec, highest priority first
  ulpf_route           one route per spec
  p_<spec>             generated VRL per spec: parse → time → fields → enums → set → derive →
                       unmapped/coverage accounting → constraint checks → status
  ulpf_fallback        unmatched / pre-parse errors / oversized / archive-integrity failures
  ulpf_failed          runtime errors inside a spec program (dropped output, rerouted)
  ulpf_finalize        OCSF metadata (uid, logged/processed time, log_format, loggers,
                       transformation_info_list), raw_data + raw_data_hash, Base Event for
                       non-parsed events, _osid = event_uid
        ├──► out_opensearch   elasticsearch sink (api v8, bulk to the write alias, id = event_uid,
        │                     own buffer: memory 50k events (default) or disk ≥ 256 MiB, drop_newest)
        ├──► ulpf_normalized_line ─► batch ─► out_normalized (file: normalized NDJSON)
        └──► ulpf_dlq_filter (fallback|failed) ─► line ─► batch ─► out_dlq (file)
  ulpf_internal_logs ─► ulpf_loss_filter (WARN/ERROR) ─► out_losses (file, recorded losses)
  ulpf_internal_metrics ─► out_metrics (Prometheus exporter 127.0.0.1:9598)
```

Design properties and the evidence for them:

| Property | How | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| raw-first | the archive branch forks from the envelope **before** any parsing; parse failures cannot prevent archiving | Scenario 4 (25 tricky payloads byte-identical), accounting PASS runs |
| lossless normalization | every source field is mapped, kept in `unmapped`, or recorded empty; runtime check `fields = mapped + unmapped + empty`; independent Python oracle in `ulpf test` | completeness check on all 31 vectors |
| no silent drops | fallback/failed are indexed + DLQ; Vector's own WARN/ERROR go to `out_losses`; `ulpf account` reconciles UIDs and SHA-256 | Scenario 10 (malformed corpus), accounting |
| outage isolation | OpenSearch sink has its own buffer that drops when full — the archive branch never back-pressures on the index | `scripts/demo_outage.py` (disk buffer: verification/outage_test.log; memory buffer: outage_test_memory_buffer.log) |
| file-sink throughput | reduce batching (≤1000 lines or ≤0.5 s per write): Vector 0.58's file sink otherwise issues one write per event | the lines stay byte-identical: accounting PASS on every run since (e.g. the 861-event live demo, docs/demo-script.md). The throughput figures measured during development (~210 events/s per-event, ~11k lines/s batched) were **not recorded** as evidence. They are UNVERIFIED until the benchmark (`make bench`) is run. |
| fast start/reload | generated VRL avoids static per-field keys that made VRL type checking quadratic | finding P4b-1 |
| safe configuration changes | hot reload only for spec changes; any other change is refused while Vector runs, or applied by a drained restart (see below) | finding P6-4, `tests/unit/test_reload.py`, `verification/reload_codec_experiment.log` |
| byte-exact retention | `ulpf lake compact` records the empty-line layout, so a pruned NDJSON file is restored with its original SHA-256 | `tests/unit/test_lake.py`, finding P6-4 |

## Control plane

| Area | Commands | Module |
|---|---|---|
| specs | `spec lint`, `spec compile [--check] [--restart]`, `test` | `spec.py`, `compile.py`, `testing.py`, `build.py` |
| onboarding | `fingerprint`, `mine`, `onboard`, `gate`, `promote` | `onboard/` |
| integrity | `keygen`, `seal [--accept-gaps]`, `verify [--expect-head]`, `raw get [--proof]` | `integrity.py` |
| accounting & repair | `account [--sendlog]`, `repair [--dry-run]` | `accounting.py`, `repair.py` |
| replay | `replay new-index|backfill|missing|rollback|status` | `replay.py` |
| quality | `drift check|baseline`, `scorecard` | `drift.py`, `scorecard.py` |
| analytics | `detect sigma|anomaly`, `anomaly`, `lake compact [--prune]|verify [--repair-layout]|restore|stats` | `detect.py`, `lake.py` |
| operator UI | `stack up ui` → <http://127.0.0.1:8501>: Overview, Live feed, Event explorer, Unknown sources & onboarding, Archive integrity, Replay, Detections | `ui/app.py`, `ui/theme.py`, `.streamlit/config.toml` |
| live demo | UI *Live feed* page; demo traffic only with `ULPF_DEMO=1` (`make demo-live`, docs/demo-script.md) | `demo.py`, `ui/app.py` |
| operations | `doctor`, `stack up|down|status [service]`, `os bootstrap|secure`, `secrets init`, `certs init`, `runtime fetch|verify|install`, `bundle lock|build [--tar]`, `gen` | `doctor.py`, `stack.py`, `os_security.py`, `credentials.py`, `runtime.py`, `bundle.py`, `gen.py` |

Versions of everything pinned (Vector, OpenSearch, plugin, Python packages):
[verification/VERSIONS.md](../verification/VERSIONS.md) and
[verification/DEPENDENCIES.md](../verification/DEPENDENCIES.md).

### One interpretation of a spec (ADR-010)

The same generated VRL runs live, in `ulpf test`, in `ulpf gate`, in replays
and in backfills: batch runs feed archive records through
`replay_envelope.vrl` (re-verifying each record's SHA-256) into the identical
parser stages. There is no second (Python) implementation of parsing that
could disagree with production; Python only provides *independent oracles*
(completeness, expectations) that check it.

### Indices and aliases

`<prefix>-v<N>` backing indices with a read alias and a write alias (with
`is_write_index`). The index template is generated from the OCSF dictionary
(type-driven dynamic templates; `unmapped` as `flat_object`; `ulpf.ingest.time`
as `date_nanos`). `action.auto_create_index: "-ulpf-*,+*"` stops accidental
untemplated indices. Replays build `v<N+1>` and move both aliases in one
`_aliases` call (Scenario 6).

### State on disk (`runtime/`, never committed)

```
runtime/data/archive/raw/<day>/raw-<bucket>-<collector>.ndjson   raw archive (bucket = archive write time)
runtime/data/archive/manifests/<seq>.json + .sig, HEAD            sealed batches (Ed25519, hash chain)
runtime/data/archive/index.sqlite                                 event_uid -> archive location
runtime/data/normalized/<day>/events-*.ndjson                     normalized NDJSON (hot; pruned after verified compaction)
runtime/data/dlq/<day>/dlq-*.ndjson, vector-internal-*.ndjson     fallback/failed copies, recorded losses
runtime/data/lake/ocsf/date=<day>/*.parquet + _manifest.json      Parquet (verified; the record for pruned NDJSON)
runtime/data/onboarding/<spec id>/                                samples, onboard.json, gate reports, archived drafts
runtime/data/state/                                               drift baselines, promotions, replays, last test
runtime/data/inbox/                                               file input (*.log)
runtime/data/vector/                                              Vector data_dir (file-source checkpoints, disk buffer if configured)
runtime/data/opensearch/                                          OpenSearch data and logs
runtime/secrets/ (0700)                                           pii.key, OpenSearch users
runtime/ulpf.local.yaml, runtime/opensearch-security.yml          written by `ulpf os secure` (security on, https)
runtime/opensearch-config/                                        rendered opensearch.yml, jvm.options, security config, certs
runtime/vector/, runtime/opensearch/, runtime/MANIFEST.json       installed binaries + their SHA-256 (`make runtime`)
runtime/dist/, runtime/wheelhouse/, runtime/sdist/                pinned downloads: the offline install sources (`make fetch`)
runtime/run/, runtime/logs/                                       PID files (and demo.json), service logs
runtime/tmp/                                                      batch/replay configs, demo sendlogs, experiments (`make clean`)
runtime/bundle/                                                   offline bundle (`make bundle`)
deploy/keys/ (seal.key 0600, release.key), deploy/certs/          signing keys, deployment CA + certificates (git-ignored)
```

## Processes, ports and lifecycle

`ulpf stack` starts each service as a child process of the invoking user, in
its own session.

| Service | Listens on (default, loopback) | Start timeout | Stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| opensearch | 9200 HTTP, 9300 transport | 300 s (the first secured start initialises the security index) | SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 60 s |
| vector | 5514 UDP/TCP, 6514 TLS, 8088 HTTP, 8686 API, 9598 metrics | 240 s (VRL type checking of all specs, P4b-1) | SIGTERM. Vector drains its buffers within its graceful-shutdown limit (120 s; Vector's default is 60 s). ulpf waits 150 s, then reports any component Vector had to kill. |
| ui | 8501 | 60 s | SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 60 s |

- **Files.** PID files are in `runtime/run/` and logs in
  `runtime/logs/<service>.log`. OpenSearch's configuration is rendered at
  every start into `runtime/opensearch-config/` from `deploy/ulpf.yaml`. It
  uses absolute disk watermarks: 1.5 GB low, 1 GB high, 600 MB flood stage.
- **Lifetime.** The services are not system services. On the reference Ubuntu
  desktop they stopped when the terminal that started them was closed, and
  they do not start at boot.

## Applying configuration changes

Vector runs with `--watch-config`; `ulpf spec compile` replaces
`vector-live.yaml` atomically, which makes Vector hot-reload.
`build.reload_hazards` compares the new configuration with the running one:

- **Spec changes reload in place.** A promotion, change or retirement only
  touches the spec programs (`p_*`), `ulpf_match`, `ulpf_route` and the input
  lists of the fan-in transforms.
- **Everything else needs a restart.** Changes to sinks or codecs, the archive
  branch, sources or global options are refused while Vector runs. The reason:
  Vector 0.58 keeps a changed sink's buffer across a hot reload, and encodes the
  events already buffered with the new settings. A json → text codec change
  turned them into empty lines and logged nothing (finding P6-4, reproduced by
  `scripts/reload_codec_experiment.sh`).
- **Drained restart.** `ulpf spec compile --restart` stops Vector, which first
  drains its buffers, writes the configuration and starts Vector again.

`ulpf promote` builds the live configuration in the same way, so a promotion
can never apply a structural change by hot reload.

## Security

| Aspect | Implementation |
|---|---|
| exposure | every listener and service on 127.0.0.1 by default. `permit_origin` (default 127.0.0.0/8) applies to TCP listeners; Vector does not support it for UDP. `ulpf doctor` fails non-loopback listeners. |
| transport | TLS syslog listener (6514) with the deployment CA (`ulpf certs init`, RSA 3072). With `ulpf os secure`, OpenSearch uses TLS on HTTP and transport; Vector verifies the certificate and host name. |
| OpenSearch access | Internal users with BCrypt hashes, created by the plugin's own hasher; the plugin's demo users are never installed. Anonymous access is off. `admin` (all_access) serves the control plane, `ulpf-writer` (bulk index into `ulpf-*`, no read or delete) serves Vector, and `ulpf-reader` (read `ulpf-*`) serves the UI and detections. The admin certificate is the only admin DN. |
| secrets | generated on the host, never committed or bundled. The OpenSearch passwords and `pii.key` live in `runtime/secrets/` (0700, files 0600). Vector reads the writer password through its secret backend, so it never appears in the generated config. |
| integrity | Ed25519 seal key (`deploy/keys/seal.key`, 0600) for archive manifests; release key for offline bundles (`BUNDLE.json.sig`) |
| PII | `pii:` fields in a spec are pseudonymised with HMAC-SHA-256 (`pii.key`) before mapping. Limitation: `raw_data` still holds the received line in clear text. |
| no outbound traffic | the processing path never contacts the internet. The optional LLM must be on localhost (`ULPF_LLM_URL`), and its suggestions stay inactive comments. Streamlit usage statistics are off. |
| UI | Streamlit on loopback, no login of its own (limitation). Only explicit actions write: run a gate, promote with a named approver, verify. |

## Failure handling summary

| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| unknown format | Base Event, `status=fallback`, generic layers in `unmapped`, DLQ, fingerprint cluster |
| spec mismatch on a field | value kept in `unmapped`, error in `ulpf.errors`, `status=partial` |
| VRL runtime error | `status=failed` (`parser_runtime_error`), raw still archived |
| oversized (> 64 KiB) | archived byte-for-byte, `status=failed`, `oversized` |
| frame > 1 MiB | discarded by Vector at framing, logged → `out_losses` (lower bound under bursts, V15) |
| OpenSearch down | archive + NDJSON continue; index buffered (memory or disk), then drained; overflow or a restart while buffering is repaired from the archive by `ulpf replay missing` |
| structural config change while Vector runs | refused; applied only with `ulpf spec compile --restart` (drained restart). Before this guard, a codec change re-encoded 1311 buffered events as empty lines (P6-4). `ulpf repair` recovered them from the index, after checking each one's SHA-256 and length. |
| Vector stopped with a backlog | drained within the 120 s graceful-shutdown limit; `ulpf stack down` reports components Vector had to kill (their events would show up in `ulpf account`) |
| archive file with empty lines | `ulpf seal` holds it back; after `ulpf account`/`ulpf repair`, `ulpf seal --accept-gaps` declares the gaps in the signed manifest; filling a gap later fails `ulpf verify` |
| disk below OpenSearch's flood stage (600 MB free) | OpenSearch refuses writes; archive and NDJSON continue; after freeing space `ulpf replay missing` re-indexes |
| launching terminal closed | the services stop (observed); `ulpf account` after a restart shows whether anything was lost in flight |

## Disk footprint (measured 2026-10-07, reference VM)

| Item | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime/opensearch` | 511 MB | OpenSearch min 3.8.0: bundled JDK 252 MB, modules 119 MB, lib 80 MB, security plugin 57 MB |
| `.venv` | 681 MB | pyarrow 156 MB, scipy 109 MB (scikit-learn), pandas 72 MB (Streamlit), scikit-learn 49 MB, numpy 43 MB, Streamlit 36 MB |
| `runtime/dist` | 346 MB | pinned Vector/OpenSearch/plugin archives — the offline install source |
| `runtime/wheelhouse` | 158 MB | every Python dependency as a wheel — the offline install source |
| `runtime/vector` | 145 MB | static musl Vector binary |
| data, per event (measured, mixed vendors) | archive 933 B, normalized NDJSON 4,960 B, Parquet 310 B (16.0x smaller than NDJSON), OpenSearch 2,071 B (primary store after force-merge) | hence `ulpf lake compact --prune` |

Kept small by design: the bundle directory hard-links `dist/` and the wheels
(`--tar` creates a real copy only when a transfer file is needed); the
air-gap test deletes its ~1.4 GB sandbox install when it ends; the index
buffer defaults to memory (a Vector disk buffer is never smaller than
256 MiB); `make clean` removes regenerable leftovers.
